response: ## Review: `src/assets/hero-banner.png` **Finding:** `crime_00011` — Oversized Raster (`oversized_raster`, universal pack), confidence 0.95. **Size, quoted from the evidence:** > `byte size: 260,000 bytes (253.9 KB)` > `severity ladder: low ≥ 200 KB · medium ≥ 500 KB · high ≥ 1000 KB` > `format: png` ### Verdict: request changes — do not block 254 KB lands in the **low** band, barely over the 200 KB floor and nowhere near the 500 KB medium line. `crimes` scores it `severity 0.4`, `effort: quick`. That isn't a merge-blocker on its own. But the context nudges it up: this is the **landing-page hero**, which means it's almost certainly the LCP element. A 254 KB LCP image is roughly 2–3× a healthy budget, and it's on the critical path for every first-time visitor. So: fix it in this PR, but as a normal review round, not a red-light block. If the landing page is behind a performance budget in CI, let that gate fail the build rather than a human veto. ### Recommended transformation **One caveat first:** the finding reports bytes and format only — no intrinsic dimensions (contrast `crime_00013`, where the detector did surface `32 × 32 px`). So I can't tell from the scan alone whether this is an oversized *encode* of a correctly-sized image or a 4000px export being downscaled by the browser. Check the intrinsic size before picking numbers; if it's wider than ~2× the largest CSS render width, the resize alone will do most of the work. **Target dimensions.** Size to the visible render area, not the design canvas: - Measure the largest CSS width the hero actually occupies (a full-bleed hero usually tops out around 1440–1600 CSS px at common desktop widths, even on a 2560px monitor, once container padding and max-width are applied). - Ship `2×` that as the largest variant — so ~2880–3200px wide only if the hero truly goes edge-to-edge; ~1600px if it's inside a 800px content column. - Serve a `srcset` ladder rather than one file: **768w / 1280w / 1920w / 2560w**, with `sizes` reflecting the real layout. Mobile then pulls ~40 KB instead of the desktop asset. - Budget: **≤ 150 KB for the largest variant, ideally under 100 KB.** That's the number to hold the PR to, not "smaller than before." **Format: AVIF primary, WebP fallback, via ``.** ```html ``` Why AVIF here specifically: - A hero banner is photographic or gradient-heavy content — exactly where AVIF's advantage is largest. At equal perceptual quality it typically lands **30–50% under WebP**, and WebP is already ~25–35% under PNG. Stacking resize + AVIF should take 254 KB to well under 80 KB. - AVIF's weakness is encode time (seconds per image, not milliseconds). Irrelevant for one build-time hero asset; it would matter for a user-upload pipeline. - AVIF also handles wide gamut and smooth gradients without the banding you'd get from PNG-8 quantization or aggressive WebP quality settings. - Support is fine for a landing page: Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari 16+. The `` fallback covers the rest at zero risk. **If the project can only carry one format** — no build pipeline, hand-managed assets — pick **WebP**. Universal support, one file, still a large win over PNG. The extra AVIF gain isn't worth a bespoke encode step in a repo that isn't set up for it. **Also worth asking:** PNG suggests the asset may have come straight out of a design tool. If the "hero" is flat color, a gradient, or geometric shapes, the right fix isn't re-encoding — it's a CSS gradient or an SVG, and the asset disappears entirely. `crimes` hints at this in the suggested action. Only if it's genuinely photographic does the resize-and-re-encode path apply. ### Blocking behaviour While the hero is being fixed, add `fetchpriority="high"`, explicit `width`/`height` (prevents CLS), and make sure it is **not** `loading="lazy"` — lazy-loading the LCP element is a common regression that costs more than the bytes do. ### Adjacent, out of scope for this PR Two sibling findings in the same asset directory, both `low`, both worth a follow-up ticket rather than scope creep here: - `crime_00013` — `src/assets/check-icon.png`, a 32×32 raster that should be SVG. - `crime_00001` — `src/assets/partner-logo.svg` (`high`, confidence 0.95) carries 2 base64-embedded rasters. That one is the higher-value fix of the three.
